parts.visual:
A team spends two years building a podcasting app. It fails miserably. But they notice that the internal chat tool they built for themselves to communicate is amazing. The PM makes a terrifying decision: they delete the podcast app entirely, and launch their internal chat tool to the public. That chat tool was called Slack.

The Evolution:
1. The Pivot: A fundamental, violent shift in the business strategy or core product when data proves the original idea is dead.
2. Sunk Cost Fallacy: The psychological trap that kills companies. Founders refuse to pivot because they 'already spent 2 years and $2 million on it'. The market does not care how hard you worked. If it is dead, you must cut it.
parts.audio: A pivot is not a failure; it is a profound realization of the truth. The most successful companies in the world did not succeed with their original idea. They succeeded with their third idea, after brutally killing the first two.

questions.question: What is the 'Sunk Cost Fallacy'?
options: The irrational desire to keep investing money and time into a failed project simply because you have already invested so much into it. A great PM ignores past costs and only makes decisions based on future potential.
questions.correct_answer: The irrational desire to keep investing money and time into a failed project simply because you have already invested so much into it. A great PM ignores past costs and only makes decisions based on future potential.
questions.explanation: You cannot refund yesterday. You can only save tomorrow.

questions.question: Listen to the founder of Instagram. What kind of Pivot did they execute?
questions.tts_text: We originally built a massive app called Burbn. It had check-ins, points, calendars, and photos. It was too confusing. But we noticed users ONLY used the photo filter feature. So we deleted 90% of the app, kept only the photos, and renamed it Instagram.
options: A 'Zoom-In' Pivot. They took one single feature of a massive, failing product, and pivoted the entire company to focus 100% on that one specific feature. Simplification saved the company.
questions.correct_answer: A 'Zoom-In' Pivot. They took one single feature of a massive, failing product, and pivoted the entire company to focus 100% on that one specific feature. Simplification saved the company.
questions.explanation: Sometimes the whole is weaker than the parts.

questions.question: Why is a Pivot terrifying for the engineering team?
options: Code Annihilation. A true pivot often means taking 100,000 lines of code that the engineers spent a year writing, and permanently deleting it. The PM must manage the immense psychological blow to the team's morale.
Because the code is too fast.
questions.correct_answer: Code Annihilation. A true pivot often means taking 100,000 lines of code that the engineers spent a year writing, and permanently deleting it. The PM must manage the immense psychological blow to the team's morale.
questions.explanation: Code is temporary. The mission is permanent.

questions.question: What is a 'Customer Pivot'?
options: The product stays exactly the same, but you realize you are selling it to the wrong people. For example, you built a task manager for teenagers (who won't pay), and you pivot to selling the exact same software to corporate lawyers (who will pay $50/month).
